reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses a design approach based on ΔG_bcc-fcc and deformation-induced martensitic transformation, but it describes an FCC-to-BCC transformation in a different alloy system (varying Co content), not the BCC-to-FCC transformation proposed for Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7. The evidence does not support the specific premises about the direction of transformation, the role of sluggish diffusion, or the predicted outcomes for this alloy.
premises: Phase stability is governed by the temperature-dependent Gibbs free energy difference (ΔG_bcc-fcc) between BCC and FCC phases.
A martensitic transformation from BCC to FCC occurs as temperature decreases, driven by ΔG_bcc-fcc.
Sluggish diffusion in multicomponent alloys delays the transformation unless sufficient time or deformation is provided.
Slow cooling or deformation will increase FCC phase fraction, while rapid quenching retains BCC.
The extent of transformation correlates with predicted ΔG_bcc-fcc values.
